title: Yaphank, Weeks Pond Settlement
summary: Yaphank, a village in Brookhaven town, was originally the name of the creek south of the hamlet. A land deed signed in 1664 by Unkechaug Sachem Tobacus mentions a river called Yamphanke. In the 17th century, the Unkechaug Indians, who had their primary residence in nearby Mastic, built temporary campsites near what was later known as Weeks Pond.
activity_update_summary: Consolidated dated history into the cited Historic Timeline so the listing no longer repeats the same content.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Unkechaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Unkechaug families whose primary residences were in Mastic regularly maintained temporary campsites near Weeks Pond along the river identified as Yamphanke in a 1664 deed. Preserving the memory of these seasonal encampments illustrates how Indigenous communities actively moved across the landscape to harvest diverse inland and coastal resources.
